title: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

blocks.tex:
We work with the classical stable category $\mathrm{Sp}$, the synthetic category $\mathrm{Syn}$, and their mod-two Adams towers. Fix a map $
u_3\colon S^3	o S$ and a pointed detecting spectrum $D$. Let $\mathcal C_0$ consist of the sphere, the cofiber of $
u_3$, $D$, and their integer suspensions. Let $\mathcal S_0$ be generated by the synthetic sphere and $
u(\mathcal C_0)$ under bidegree shifts and finite $\lambda$ quotients. Convergence assertions below are restricted to these object families unless further hypotheses are stated.

In the statements quoted from \cite{LWX126}, spectra are assumed to be $2$-completed, connective, and of finite type. Original numbering and context are available in \href{paper/main.tex.html}{the source text} and \href{paper/2412.10879.pdf}{the paper}.

comments.title: Module interface conventions
comments.text:
Module-level interface conventions; completion remains derived from verified Lean evidence.

- **principle**: 普通公共导入即可调用同一固定背景上的对象与定理；下游不传入结果包。保留真正数学前提；未完成构造与证明逐项登记，不能把可调用误报为已证明。

- **type_authority**: Complete types and universe/typeclass assumptions live in the referenced Lean declarations. The API manifest and normal-import tests freeze their elaborated types; this semantic ledger is not a second Lean source registry.

- **exclusions**: README and AGENTS edits

- **exclusions**: Blueprint migration/checks

- **exclusions**: Literature/Computation/ProofTools/Main implementations

- **exclusions**: raw CSV/Generated/checkers

- **exclusions**: full completion-model identification and derived-source unitor are explicit unfinished source tasks

- **weight_direction_correction.statement**: For w1≤w2≤t, the quotient and actual lambda map lower weight w2→w1.

- **weight_direction_correction.reason**: B_(1+t-w2) ≤ B_(1+t-w1); the old reverse quotient map was not well-defined in general.

- **weight_direction_correction.affected_type**: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.NuInfinityWeightMaps

- **weight_direction_correction.compatibility**: Intentional signature correction; former type freeze updated and tracking retained.

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.statement**: NuExactTriangleInput requires injectivity, middle exactness and surjectivity in every HF2-homology degree.

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.reason**: Middle exactness of a distinguished triangle alone does not imply that nu preserves its cofiber.

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.affected_type**: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.NuExactTriangleInput.preserves

- **nu_cofiber_condition_correction.compatibility**: Intentional correction of an overly strong legacy input; the same predicate is reused by the full Literature iff.

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:nu-exactness
blocks.title: When nu preserves a cofiber triangle
blocks.body:
Let $X	o Y	o Z	o\Sigma X$ be a distinguished triangle in $\mathrm{Sp}$. If its mod-two homology forms a short exact sequence in every degree, then there exists $h\colon
u Z	o\Sigma
u X$ such that $
u X	o
u Y	o
u Z\xrightarrow{h}\Sigma
u X$ is a distinguished triangle in $\mathrm{Syn}$.

        (shiftFunctor SyntheticSpectrum (1 : ℤ)).obj (nu.functor.obj T.obj₁),
      CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk
        (nu.functor.map T.mor₁) (nu.functor.map T.mor₂) h ∈ distTriang SyntheticSpectrum := by
  sorry

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:finite-separation
blocks.title: Separation for maps of finite spectra
blocks.body: Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a map between finite spectra. If $f$ lies in every integer stage of the Adams filtration, then $f$ is odd torsion. The same assertion holds for the factorization filtration. Consequently, every map between finite spectra which is not odd torsion has an exact finite integer filtration.

blocks.title: Low-filtration support and sphere separation
blocks.body: For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, one has $E_r^{s,t}(X)=0$ whenever $s<0$. For the sphere, $E_r^{0,t}(S)=0$ for every nonzero $t\geq0$. A sphere homotopy class lying in $F^s$ for every $s\in\mathbb N$ is odd torsion.

lean.code:
public theorem sphere_page_filtration_zero (r : ℤ) (t : ℕ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    Subsingleton (model.classical.sphere.Page r (0,t)) := by
  let T := model.classicalTower.tower (SphereSpectrum (C := Spectrum))
  let e : T.layer 0 ≅ model.coefficients.object :=
    T.layerIso 0 ≪≫ (tensorLeft model.coefficients.object).mapIso T.zeroIso ≪≫
      ρ_ model.coefficients.object
  letI := model.coefficients.homotopy_vanishes (t : ℤ) (by exact_mod_cast ht)
  letI : Subsingleton (T.FirstPage (0,t)) := by
    change Subsingleton (HomotopyGroup (t : ℤ) (T.layer 0))
    exact (Iso.homCongr (Iso.refl (Sphere (C := Spectrum) (t : ℤ))) e).injective.subsingleton
  let D := model.classical.sphere.ssData (0,t)
  letI : Subsingleton D.V :=
    (model.classicalTower.sequence (SphereSpectrum (C := Spectrum))).ambient (0,t)
      |>.toLinearEquiv.injective.subsingleton
  exact page_subsingleton_of_ambient D _

public theorem classical_page_negative (X : ClassicalObject) (r s t : ℤ)
    (hs : s < 0) :
    Subsingleton ((model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).Page r (s,t)) := by
  let T := model.classicalTower.tower (X.obj model.auxiliary)
  have hi (a b : ℕ) (hab : a ≤ b) (h : a = b) : IsIso (T.map hab) := by
    subst b
    rw [T.map_self]
    infer_instance
  let f := T.mapAt (show s ≤ s+1 by omega)
  haveI : IsIso f := hi s.toNat (s+1).toNat (by omega) (by omega)
  have hLayer : IsZero (T.layer s) :=
    Pretriangulated.Triangle.isZero₃_of_isIso₁
      (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk f (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibι f)
        (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibδ f))
      (HasFunctorialCofiber.cofib_distinguished f) (show IsIso f from inferInstance)
  letI : Subsingleton (T.FirstPage (s,t)) := ⟨fun a b => hLayer.eq_of_tgt a b⟩
  let D := (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).ssData (s,t)
  letI : Subsingleton D.V :=
    (model.classicalTower.sequence (X.obj model.auxiliary)).ambient (s,t)
      |>.toLinearEquiv.injective.subsingleton
  exact page_subsingleton_of_ambient D _

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:homology-exact
blocks.title: Cofiber homology and a cardinality bound
blocks.body: Mod-two homology of a cofiber sequence is exact at the cofiber term, with boundary induced by the cofiber map to the suspension. Suppose that every finite subset of the two adjacent homology groups has cardinality at most $n_X$ and $n_Y$, respectively. Then every finite subset of the cofiber homology group has cardinality at most $n_Xn_Y$.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.homology_exact
lean.code:
public theorem homology_exact (T : HoCofiberSequence (C := Spectrum)) (i : ℤ) :
    Function.Exact (modTwoHomologyMap coefficients T.g i)
      (modTwoConnecting coefficients homologyShift T i) := by
  let U := Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk (coefficients.object ◁ T.f)
    (coefficients.object ◁ T.g) (coefficients.object ◁ T.h ≫ (homologyShift T.X).hom)
  have hU : U ∈ distTriang Spectrum := homology_triangle_distinguished T
  intro z
  change AbstractAdamsTower.desuspend (coefficients.object ⊗ T.X) i
    (z ≫ U.mor₃) = 0 ↔ ∃ y, y ≫ U.mor₂ = z
  have hzero : AbstractAdamsTower.desuspend (coefficients.object ⊗ T.X) i
      (z ≫ U.mor₃) = 0 ↔ z ≫ U.mor₃ = 0 := by
    constructor
    · intro hz
      apply desuspend_injective (coefficients.object ⊗ T.X) i
      simpa only [map_zero] using hz
    · intro hz
      rw [hz, map_zero]
  rw [hzero]
  constructor
  · intro hz
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := Pretriangulated.Triangle.coyoneda_exact₃ U hU z hz
    exact ⟨y, hy.symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
    rw [Category.assoc, Pretriangulated.comp_distTriang_mor_zero₂₃ U hU, comp_zero]

- **constraints**: Localization descent requires the entire spectral sequence to invert the explicit HF₂ Hom-test equivalences.

- **constraints**: Full source unitor normalization and comparison with the paper's completion remain explicit unformalized backlog.

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:milnor-products
blocks.title: The sphere product in Milnor cohomology
blocks.body: The Milnor equivalence identifies the sphere $E_2$ product with the normalized cobar cup product and sends the sphere unit to the cohomology unit. The sphere product satisfies the corresponding commutativity law.

public theorem sphereProduct_milnor (s t s' t' : ℕ)
    (x : classical.sphere.Page 2 ((s : ℤ), (t : ℤ)))
    (y : classical.sphere.Page 2 ((s' : ℤ), (t' : ℤ))) :
    sphereE2_milnorEquiv (s + s') (t + t')
      ((eqToHom (congrArg (classical.sphere.Page 2)
        (show ((s : ℤ), (t : ℤ)) + ((s' : ℤ), (t' : ℤ)) =
          (((s + s' : ℕ) : ℤ), ((t + t' : ℕ) : ℤ)) by
            ext <;> simp)))
        (sphereAlgebra.product _ _ x y)) =
      milnorCup (sphereE2_milnorEquiv s t x) (sphereE2_milnorEquiv s' t' y) := by
  sorry

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.standardH6Square_milnor
lean.code:
public theorem standardH6Square_milnor :
    sphereE2_milnorEquiv 2 128 standardH6Square = milnorHiSquareClass 6 := by
  have h := sphereProduct_milnor 1 64 1 64 standardH6 standardH6
  simp only [standardH6Square_eq_product] at ⊢
  change sphereE2_milnorEquiv 2 128
    (sphereAlgebra.product (1,64) (1,64) standardH6 standardH6) = _
  change sphereE2_milnorEquiv 2 128
    (sphereAlgebra.product (1,64) (1,64) standardH6 standardH6) = _ at h
  rw [h]
  have hh : sphereE2_milnorEquiv 1 64 standardH6 = milnorHiClass 6 :=
    standardHi_milnor 6
  rw [hh]
  exact (Milnor.hiSquare_eq_cup 6).symm
lean.statement:
public theorem standardH6Square_milnor :
    sphereE2_milnorEquiv 2 128 standardH6Square = milnorHiSquareClass 6

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-detection
blocks.title: Detection of maps in the mapping spectral sequence
blocks.body: For finite spectra $X,Y$, the Adams filtration of $f\colon X\to Y$ equals that of its class in $\pi_0F(X,Y)$. Exact filtration is detected by the convergence quotient comparison. If $f$ is not odd torsion, it has a nonzero $E_\infty$ detector represented by a common infinite cycle.

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-pairing
blocks.title: Composition pairings of mapping sequences
blocks.body: For finite spectra $X,Y,Z$, composition induces a converging pairing from the Adams sequences of $F(X,Y)$ and $F(Y,Z)$ to that of $F(X,Z)$. Its parity is the Adams stem parity, and its abutment pairing is shifted composition in $\mathrm{Sp}$.

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-laws
blocks.title: Associativity and units for mapping composition
blocks.body: The finite-page mapping pairings are associative under the degree identifications and have compatible left and right units. Each unit is represented by a common infinite cycle whose abutment is the identity map.

comments.title: Interface scope: standard-sphere-classes
comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `standard-sphere-classes`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: 同一实际球谱E₂的F₂乘法及指定标准h_i，平方使用该乘法。

- **constraints**: The existing standardHi construction is retained. Its separately registered identity theorem fixes it to the specified ξ₁^(2^i) class through the same actual E₁/d₁/E₂ descent diagram.

- **constraints**: The E₂ comparison must descend the actual tower coordinates, rather than be an unrelated graded linear equivalence.

- **constraints**: The actual sphere product and unit must agree with the independently defined cobar cup product and unit.

- **constraints**: No uniqueness or nonvanishing of the entire h_i family is assumed; h6-square nonvanishing is separate.

- **constraints**: No permanent-survival conclusion is an AdamsSynthetic input.

- **roles**: data

- **roles**: operation

- **roles**: structural-law

blocks.title: Enriched composition agrees on all three layers
blocks.body: On elementary products, enriched composition agrees with the mapping composition pairing on every finite page, on $E_\infty$, and on the abutment. The enriched identities agree with the mapping units on each of these three levels.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.mappingEnriched_composition_abutment

public theorem mappingEnriched_composition_abutment : letI := mappingEnriched_monoidal
    ∀ (X Y Z : MappingObject (IsFiniteSpectrum (C := Spectrum))) (i j : ℤ)

public theorem mappingEnriched_composition_eInfty : letI := mappingEnriched_monoidal
    ∀ (X Y Z : MappingObject (IsFiniteSpectrum (C := Spectrum))) (i j : ℤ × ℤ)
      (x : ((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).eInfty)
      (y : ((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).eInfty),
      let f : (mappingSystem.hom X Y ⊗ mappingSystem.hom Y Z) ⟶ mappingSystem.hom X Z :=
        eqToHom (congrArg₂ (fun A B : ConvergingSequence.{0,0} ℤ => A ⊗ B)
          (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Y).symm (mappingEnriched_hom_eq Y Z).symm) ≫ mappingEnriched_enriched.comp X Y Z ≫
            eqToHom (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Z)
      f.sequence.eInftyMap (i+j) ((mappingEnriched_tensorPairing X Y Z).eInftyPair i j x y) =
        (mappingComposition.pairing X Y Z).eInftyPair i j x y := by
  letI := mappingEnriched_monoidal
  intro X Y Z i j x y
  let f : (mappingSystem.hom X Y ⊗ mappingSystem.hom Y Z) ⟶ mappingSystem.hom X Z :=
    eqToHom (congrArg₂ (fun A B : ConvergingSequence.{0,0} ℤ => A ⊗ B)
      (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Y).symm (mappingEnriched_hom_eq Y Z).symm) ≫
        mappingEnriched_enriched.comp X Y Z ≫ eqToHom (mappingEnriched_hom_eq X Z)
  let P := mappingEnriched_tensorPairing X Y Z
  let Q := mappingComposition.pairing X Y Z
  haveI : Epi (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Epi (cokernel.π _))
  haveI : Epi (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Epi (cokernel.π _))
  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective
    (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤)).mp inferInstance x
  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective
    (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤)).mp inferInstance y
  have h₀ (U V : MappingObject (IsFiniteSpectrum (C := Spectrum))) :
      (mappingSystem.hom U V).underlying.E.r₀ ≤ 2 :=
    le_of_eq (classical.firstPage _)
  have hT : (mappingSystem.hom X Y ⊗ mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.r₀ ≤ 2 :=
    f.sequence.r₀_eq.le.trans (h₀ X Z)
  have h := mappingEnriched_composition_page X Y Z 2 i j
    (infinityToPage _ 2 i a) (infinityToPage _ 2 j b)
  change f.sequence.pageMap 2 (i+j)
      (P.ssPairing.pair 2 i j (infinityToPage _ 2 i a) (infinityToPage _ 2 j b)) =
    Q.ssPairing.pair 2 i j (infinityToPage _ 2 i a) (infinityToPage _ 2 j b) at h
  rw [P.finitePagePair_compatible 2 i j (h₀ X Y) (h₀ Y Z) hT,
    infinityToPage_naturality,
    Q.finitePagePair_compatible 2 i j (h₀ X Y) (h₀ Y Z) (h₀ X Z)] at h
  have hinf := ((mappingSystem.hom X Z).underlying.E.ssData (i+j)).infinity_projection_eq_of_page_projection_eq
    ↑(2 - (mappingSystem.hom X Z).underlying.E.r₀).toNat
    (f.sequence.toSSDataMorphism.cycleMap (i+j) ⊤ (P.cyclePairAtInfinity i j a b))
    (Q.cyclePairAtInfinity i j a b) h
  have htop := congrArg (fun m => m (P.cyclePairAtInfinity i j a b))
    (f.sequence.toSSDataMorphism.pageπ_pageMap (i+j) ⊤)
  change f.sequence.eInftyMap (i+j)
      (P.eInftyPair i j (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤ a)
        (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤ b)) =
    Q.eInftyPair i j (((mappingSystem.hom X Y).underlying.E.ssData i).pageπ ⊤ a)
      (((mappingSystem.hom Y Z).underlying.E.ssData j).pageπ ⊤ b)
  rw [← P.eInftyPair_induced, ← Q.eInftyPair_induced]
  exact htop.trans hinf

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:graded-hom
blocks.title: Weight-graded synthetic hom groups
blocks.body: For synthetic spectra $X,Y$, put $\operatorname{Hom}_w(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Sigma^{0,w}X,Y)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_*(X,Y)=\bigoplus_w\operatorname{Hom}_w(X,Y)$. The total hom group is a $\mathbb Z[\lambda]$-module; multiplication by $\lambda$ lowers weight by one through the shift comparison.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.graded_lambda_smul
lean.code:
public theorem graded_lambda_smul : ∀ (X Y : SyntheticSpectrum) (w : ℤ) (f : WeightHom X Y w),
    letI := graded_module X Y
    (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • weightHomInclusion w f =
      weightHomInclusion (w-1) (weightHomLambda f) := by
  intro X Y w f
  letI := graded_module X Y
  change (Polynomial.eval₂ (Int.castRingHom _) (totalLambda X Y) Polynomial.X) _ = _
  rw [Polynomial.eval₂_X]
  exact totalLambda_of X Y w f

lean.code:
@[implicit_reducible] public def graded_module : ∀ X Y : SyntheticSpectrum, Module (Polynomial ℤ) (TotalWeightHom X Y) := by
  intro X Y
  exact
    (fun (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] (D : M →+ M) =>
      let A := Module.End ℤ M
      letI : Ring A := inferInstance
      let ring : NonAssocRing A := inferInstance
      letI : Module A M := inferInstance
      let L : A := D.toIntLinearMap
      let hom : Polynomial ℤ →+* A :=
        Polynomial.eval₂RingHom' (Int.castRingHom A) L
          (fun a => @Int.cast_commute A ring a L)
      Module.compHom M hom)
      (TotalWeightHom X Y)
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid fun w =>
        (weightHomInclusion (w-1)).comp
          (Preadditive.leftComp Y
            (weightHomLambda (X := X) (𝟙 ((SyntheticCategory.biShift (0,w)).obj X)))))

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:graded-composition
blocks.title: Composition in the weight-graded enrichment
blocks.body: Composition on the weight-graded hom groups is $\mathbb Z[\lambda]$-bilinear. On homogeneous summands it is shifted composition. Under the coherent shift identifications, it is associative and the identity maps are left and right units.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.graded_compose_homogeneous
lean.code:
public theorem graded_compose_homogeneous : ∀ (X Y Z : SyntheticSpectrum) (a b : ℤ)
      (f : WeightHom X Y a) (g : WeightHom Y Z b),
    graded_compose X Y Z (weightHomInclusion b g) (weightHomInclusion a f) =
      weightHomInclusion (a+b) (weightHomComp f g) := by
  intro X Y Z a b f g
  exact totalComp_of X Y Z a b f g

      (f : WeightHom X Y a) (g : WeightHom Y Z b),
    graded_compose X Y Z (weightHomInclusion b g) (weightHomInclusion a f) =
      weightHomInclusion (a+b) (weightHomComp f g)

lean.code:
@[no_expose] public def graded_compose : ∀ X Y Z : SyntheticSpectrum,
    letI := graded_module X Y
    letI := graded_module Y Z
    letI := graded_module X Z
    TotalWeightHom Y Z →ₗ[Polynomial ℤ]
      TotalWeightHom X Y →ₗ[Polynomial ℤ] TotalWeightHom X Z := by
  intro X Y Z
  letI := graded_module X Y
  letI := graded_module Y Z
  letI := graded_module X Z
  let C : TotalWeightHom Y Z →+ (TotalWeightHom X Y →+ TotalWeightHom X Z) :=
    totalComp X Y Z
  let F : TotalWeightHom Y Z →+ (TotalWeightHom X Y →ₗ[Polynomial ℤ] TotalWeightHom X Z) :=
    { toFun := fun g =>
        { toFun := C g
          map_add' := (C g).map_add
          map_smul' := by
            intro p f
            apply additive_polynomial_smul (C g) (fun f => ?_) p f
            change totalComp X Y Z g ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • f) =
              (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • totalComp X Y Z g f
            rw [graded_X_smul, graded_X_smul]
            exact totalComp_lambda_right X Y Z f g }
      map_zero' := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro f
        exact congrArg (fun h : TotalWeightHom X Y →+ TotalWeightHom X Z => h f) (map_zero (totalComp X Y Z))
      map_add' := by
        intro g g'
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro f
        exact congrArg (fun h : TotalWeightHom X Y →+ TotalWeightHom X Z => h f) ((totalComp X Y Z).map_add g g') }
  exact
    { toFun := F
      map_add' := F.map_add
      map_smul' := by
        intro p g
        apply additive_polynomial_smul F (fun g => ?_) p g
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro f
        change totalComp X Y Z ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • g) f =
          (Polynomial.X : Polynomial ℤ) • totalComp X Y Z g f
        rw [graded_X_smul, graded_X_smul]
        exact totalComp_lambda_left X Y Z f g }

comments.title: Interface scope: obligation-zlambda-enrichment
comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `obligation-zlambda-enrichment`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: Hom 分量就是 Hom(Σ^(0,w) X,Y)，总 Hom 是这些实际 Hom 的直和；不是任意新选对象。 Polynomial.X 在直和注入上等于由同一 lam 和同一 shift comparison 构成的 weightHomLambda；权重降低一。 复合是 ℤ[λ] 双线性，齐次分量上的复合等于实际移位映射复合；单位由同一 biShift_zero 得到。 修正旧未分次 EnrichedCategory(ModuleCat ℤ[λ]) 的语义：普通 Syn 是分次富集的零次部分；不宣称 λ 是固定权重 Hom 上的自映射。 结合律和左右单位律从同一 shift coherence、齐次实际复合相容式及 DirectSum 加法归纳推导，已经删除重复输入字段。

- **constraints**: Hom 分量就是 Hom(Σ^(0,w) X,Y)，总 Hom 是这些实际 Hom 的直和；不是任意新选对象。 Polynomial.X 在直和注入上等于由同一 lam 和同一 shift comparison 构成的 weightHomLambda；权重降低一。 复合是 ℤ[λ] 双线性，齐次分量上的复合等于实际移位映射复合；单位由同一 biShift_zero 得到。 修正旧未分次 EnrichedCategory(ModuleCat ℤ[λ]) 的语义：普通 Syn 是分次富集的零次部分；不宣称 λ 是固定权重 Hom 上的自映射。 结合律和左右单位律从同一 shift coherence、齐次实际复合相容式及 DirectSum 加法归纳推导，已经删除重复输入字段。

- **constraints**: 旧未分次富集声明没有绑定权重；新合同在 ⨁ w, Hom(Σ^(0,w) X,Y) 上交付 ℤ[λ] 富集，并将普通 Syn 解释为零次部分。λ 降权一，不能在固定权重 Hom 内强行当作自映射。

- **constraints**: User-approved exception: graded_compose is no_expose; its mathematical signature and homogeneous formula remain available, and the frozen graded_compose._proof_1 full type/name must remain exact. No other new public support declaration is authorized.

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:e2-comparison
blocks.title: The classical-to-synthetic second-page comparison
blocks.body: The classical-to-synthetic comparison identifies classical $E_2$ classes with synthetic $E_2$ classes at the corresponding weights. The image of the corresponding synthetic $E_2$ label under the quotient page map detects the first $\lambda$-quotient homotopy class. For the sphere, this identification is compatible with the quotient map and powers of $\lambda$ through their detection identities.

lean.code:
public theorem sphere_first_quotient : ∀ (s t : ℤ) (x : classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t)),
    Detects (convergence (.quotient 1 .sphere)) (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl S_0_0 1) 2 (s,t,t)
        (by simpa only [SyntheticAdamsFamily.sphere, SyntheticAdamsSS.Page,
          Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x))
      ((sphereFirstQuotient nu quotients.functoriality firstQuotient s t).symm x) := by
  intro s t x
  let Z := (SyntheticCategory.biShift (0,0)).obj (nu.functor.obj SphereSpectrum)
  let e : Z ≅ (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) :=
    SyntheticCategory.biShift_zero.app _ ≪≫ nu.unitIso
  let q := (quotients.functoriality.functor 1).mapIso e
  let u0 : (family.obj Z).Page 2 (s,t,t+0) := by
    simpa only [Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero, ClassicalObject.obj] using
      comparison.nuE2 .sphere 0 s t 0 x
  let u := trPage (Int.add_zero t) u0
  let b0 := (firstQuotient .sphere 0 s t).symm x
  let b := trHom (Int.add_zero t) b0
  have hd0 := first_quotient .sphere 0 s t x
  have hd : KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Detects
      (convergence (.quotient 1 (.shift (0,0) (.nu .sphere)))) (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) 2 (s,t,t) u) b := by
    have ht := detects_tr _ (Int.add_zero t) hd0
    have htr := pageMap_tr family (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) (Int.add_zero t) u0
    exact htr ▸ ht
  let M := Classical.choice (canonical_convergence_natural syntheticTower q.hom
    (convergence (.quotient 1 (.shift (0,0) (.nu .sphere))))
    (convergence (.quotient 1 .sphere)))
  have hm := detects_map M (s,t,t) hd
  have hn : family.pageMap e.hom 2 (s,t,t) u =
      (by simpa only [SyntheticAdamsFamily.sphere, SyntheticAdamsSS.Page,
        Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x) := by
    let un0 : (family.obj Z).Page 2 (s,t,t-(0 : ℕ)) := by
      simpa only [add_zero, ClassicalObject.obj] using comparison.nuE2 .sphere 0 s t 0 x
    have h0 := comparison.sphere_nu s t 0 x
    change family.pageMap e.hom 2 (s,t,t-(0 : ℕ)) un0 = comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x at h0
    have ht := congrArg (trPage (F := family) (X := (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum))
      (s := s) (t := t) (show t-(0 : ℕ) = t by simp)) h0
    have htr := pageMap_tr family e.hom (show t-(0 : ℕ) = t by simp) un0
    rw [htr] at ht
    simpa only [u, u0, un0, trPage, eq_mp_eq_cast, cast_cast, id_eq] using ht
  have hp : family.pageMap q.hom 2 (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) 2 (s,t,t) u) =
      family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl S_0_0 1) 2 (s,t,t)
        (by simpa only [SyntheticAdamsFamily.sphere, SyntheticAdamsSS.Page,
          Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using comparison.sphereE2 s t 0 x) := by
    change (family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1) 2 (s,t,t) ≫
      family.pageMap q.hom 2 (s,t,t)) u = _
    rw [← familyPageMap_comp]
    change family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl Z 1 ≫ XModLambdaN.map e.hom 1) 2 (s,t,t) u = _
    rw [← XModLambdaN.incl_naturality, familyPageMap_comp]
    change family.pageMap (XModLambdaN.incl S_0_0 1) 2 (s,t,t)
      (family.pageMap e.hom 2 (s,t,t) u) = _
    rw [hn]
  have hb : b ≫ q.hom = (sphereFirstQuotient nu quotients.functoriality firstQuotient s t).symm x := by
    have hcast := linearEquiv_cast_symm
      (A := fun w => BiHom (t-s) w (XModLambdaN Z 1))
      (Int.add_zero t) (firstQuotient .sphere 0 s t) x
    exact (congrArg (fun z : BiHom (t-s) t (XModLambdaN Z 1) => z ≫ q.hom) hcast).symm
  exact hp ▸ hb ▸ hm

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:normalized-map
blocks.title: Normalized synthetic maps
blocks.body: For a map $f$ between objects of $\mathcal C_0$, its normalized synthetic lift is obtained from $\nu(f)$ with exponent determined by whether $f$ factors through the first stage of the target Adams tower. Composing this lift with the corresponding power of $\lambda$ gives $\nu(f)$. Every map between objects of $\mathcal S_0$ induces a morphism of converging Adams sequences.

comments.title: Interface scope: normalized-extension-language
comments.text:
Scope of the related interface family `normalized-extension-language`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: 同一actual map的归一化lift及有限/无限延拓见证；未输入传播定理。

- **constraints**: ExtensionEquation is the actual two-term filtered-map solution fiber.

- **constraints**: The full target coset uses the actual shorter-extension boundary subobject, not a selected finite subset.

- **constraints**: Length-zero extension must be derived from the same actual map on E-infinity and canonical convergence naturality.

- **constraints**: Finite witnesses retain page>=2, lower/upper length bounds, source/target cycle levels and common infinity representatives.

- **constraints**: Infinite witnesses retain common permanent representatives and the normalized lower length bound.

- **constraints**: Bounded ESS hypotheses remain separate from general unbounded extension equations.

- **roles**: data

- **roles**: predicate

- **roles**: derived-theorem

- **mathematical_review.finite_cycle_translation**: IsCycle(level) is translated to ReachesPage(level+1). Thus source page r and target page r-n+e retain the old r-1 and r-1-n+e cycle levels. Target page >=2 follows from length_upper.

- **mathematical_review.permanent_translation**: Old permanentCycles is the range of the common Z-infinity representative into E2; IsPermanentCycle preserves that semantics including zero.

- **mathematical_review.normalization**: e(f)=1 iff the same actual target tower admits a stage-one factorization, otherwise zero; no independently supplied filtration integer.

- **mathematical_review.homology_exactness**: NuExactTriangleInput uses the actual inducedMap (H.object whiskerLeft f); complete injective/exact/surjective conditions correct the old middle-only premise.

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:weight-functoriality
blocks.title: Functoriality and naturality of weight maps
blocks.body: Weight-lowering maps are identities at equal weights and compose along ordered weights. For $w_1\leq w_2\leq t$, they commute with the $E_\infty$ maps induced by $\nu(f)$.

blocks.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:shift-representatives
blocks.title: Shift transport of common representatives
blocks.body: Let $r\geq2$ be a finite page. Under the synthetic shift comparison, two shifted classes have a common representative if and only if the corresponding unshifted classes do, using the induced filtered map on homotopy groups.

lean.name: KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.shift_representative_iff
lean.code:
public theorem shift_representative_iff (δ : ℤ × ℤ) : ∀ (X : SyntheticObject) (r : ℤ) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
      (p : ℤ × ℤ) (s : ℤ)
      (x : (model.family.obj (X.obj model.nu model.auxiliary)).Page r (s,p.1+s,p.2))
      (z : ((model.family.obj (X.obj model.nu model.auxiliary)).sequence.ssData (s,p.1+s,p.2)).eInfty),
    HasInfinityRepresentative _ r (s,p.1+s,p.2) x z ↔
      HasInfinityRepresentative _ r (s,(p+δ).1+s,(p+δ).2)
        (((shift_page δ) X r hr p s).hom x)
        ((towerInfinityIso (model.convergence X) (model.convergence (.shift δ X))
          ((shift_filtered δ) X p) s).hom z) := by sorry

blocks.label: paper:3.3
blocks.title: The class $\lambda$ and its cofibers
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 3.3.)
                          
[{\cite{Pst} ([Definition 4.27])}]
    The natural comparison map
    $$S^{0,-1}=\Sus \nu (S^{-1})\to \nu(\Sus S^{-1})=S^{0,0}$$
    in the category of $\HF$-synthetic spectra is denoted by $\lambda\in \pi_{0,-1}S^{0,0}$. We denote by $S^{0,0}/\lambda$ the cofiber of $\lambda$. In general for synthetic $X$ the following
    $$\lambda\wedge id_X: \Sus^{0,-1}X\to X.$$
    is a natural transformation and by abuse of notation this map is also denoted by $\lambda$.
    We denote by $X/\lambda$ the cofiber of $\lambda$
    which is equivalent to $(S^{0,0}/\lambda) \wedge X$.

lean.name: KIP126.Synthetic.Context.SyntheticCategory
lean.code:
public class SyntheticCategory (Syn : Type u) extends
    StableHomotopyCategory.{u, v} Syn where
  biShift : ℤ × ℤ → Syn ⥤ Syn
  biShift_comp : ∀ (a b : ℤ × ℤ),
    biShift a ⋙ biShift b ≅ biShift (a + b)
  biShift_zero : biShift (0, 0) ≅ 𝟭 Syn
  biShift_compat : ∀ n : ℤ, biShift (n, 0) ≅ shiftFunctor Syn n
  /-- Each bigraded suspension is fully faithful (the inverse suspension is
      supplied by the same coherence data in a concrete model). -/
  biShift_fullyFaithful : ∀ p : ℤ × ℤ, (biShift p).FullyFaithful
  lam : biShift (0, -1) ⟶ 𝟭 Syn
  biShift_tensor_comm : ∀ (p : ℤ × ℤ) (X Y : Syn),
    (biShift p).obj (MonoidalCategory.tensorObj X Y) ≅
      MonoidalCategory.tensorObj ((biShift p).obj X) Y

The parent class supplies the additive, shifted, monoidal, and triangulated

lean.name: KIP126.Synthetic.Context.lambdaPow
lean.code:
public noncomputable def lambdaPow : (n : ℕ) → (X : Syn) →
    (SyntheticCategory.biShift (0, -(n : ℤ))).obj X ⟶ X
  | 0, X => SyntheticCategory.biShift_zero.hom.app X
  | n + 1, X => by
      have step1 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -1) ⋙
            SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).map
            (SyntheticCategory.lam.app X) ≫ lambdaPow n X
      have step2 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0, -1) + (0, -(n : ℤ)))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift_comp (0, -1) (0, -(n : ℤ))).inv.app X ≫ step1
      have heq :
          ((0 : ℤ), (-1 : ℤ)) + ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ)) =
            ((0 : ℤ), -(↑(n + 1) : ℤ)) := by
        simp
      exact heq ▸ step2
lean.statement:

  | n + 1, X => by
      have step1 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -1) ⋙
            SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ))).map
            (SyntheticCategory.lam.app X) ≫ lambdaPow n X
      have step2 :
          (SyntheticCategory.biShift ((0, -1) + (0, -(n : ℤ)))).obj X ⟶ X :=
        (SyntheticCategory.biShift_comp (0, -1) (0, -(n : ℤ))).inv.app X ≫ step1
      have heq :
          ((0 : ℤ), (-1 : ℤ)) + ((0 : ℤ), -(n : ℤ)) =
            ((0 : ℤ), -(↑(n + 1) : ℤ)) := by
        simp
      exact heq ▸ step2
lean.docstring:
The `n`-fold composite of the deformation map `λ` on `X`.

The recursive definition follows the coherence isomorphism supplied by
`biShift_comp`; in particular `lambdaPow 0 X` is the chosen identity
isomorphism from `Σ^(0,0)X` to `X`.

blocks.label: paper:2.3
blocks.title: Extensions and essential extensions
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 2.3.)
                          

    We say there is an $f$-extension from $x\in E_\infty^{s,t}(X)$ to $y\in E_\infty^{s+n,t+n}(Y)$ if $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ in the $f$-ESS. We say this $f$-extension is $\textbf{essential}$ if $y$ is nontrivial in the $E_n$-page of the $f$-ESS, or equivalently $$y\notin \BESS{f}^{s+n,t+n}_{n-1}(Y).$$
    Otherwise we refer to it as inessential.

lean.name: KIP126.Core.SpectralSequence.FilteredMapExtension.mem_indeterminacy_iff
lean.code:
public theorem mem_indeterminacy_iff :
    z ∈ TargetIndeterminacy f k s n T ↔
      0 ≤ n ∧ ∃ (a : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (F.F (s + 1) k))
        (b : T ⟶ Subobject.underlying.obj (G.F (s + n) k)),
        b ≫ G.toAssociatedGraded (s + n) k = z ∧
        a ≫ (F.F (s + 1) k).arrow ≫ f.map k =
          b ≫ (G.F (s + n) k).arrow := by
  let i := Subobject.ofLE (F.F (s + 1) k) (F.F s k) (F.mono s k)
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hn, a, b, ha, hb, he⟩
    have ha0 : a ≫ cokernel.π i = 0 := ha
    let a' := Abelian.monoLift i a ha0
    have ha' : a' ≫ i = a := Abelian.monoLift_comp i a ha0
    refine ⟨hn, a', b, hb, ?_⟩
    rw [← ha'] at he
    simpa only [Category.assoc, i, Subobject.ofLE_arrow_assoc] using he
  · rintro ⟨hn, a, b, hb, he⟩
    refine ⟨hn, a ≫ i, b, ?_, hb, ?_⟩
    · change (a ≫ i) ≫ cokernel.π i = 0
      rw [Category.assoc, cokernel.condition, comp_zero]
    · simpa only [Category.assoc, i, Subobject.ofLE_arrow_assoc] using he

blocks.title: Classical and synthetic second-page comparisons
blocks.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, $a,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, and $k\in\mathbb N$, there are linear isomorphisms
\[
K_{X,a,k}\colon E_2^{s,t}(X)\cong E_2^{s,t,t+a-k}(\Sigma^{0,a}\nu X),\qquad
K_{S,k}\colon E_2^{s,t}(S)\cong E_2^{s,t,t-k}(S^{0,0}).
\]
They commute with maps between objects of $\mathcal C_0$. The sphere comparison agrees with the $X=S$, $a=0$ comparison under $\nu S\cong S^{0,0}$, and the map induced by $\lambda$ sends $K_{X,-1,k}(x)$ to $K_{X,0,k+1}(x)$.

blocks.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:9a4b26f47efd
blocks.title: Classical convergence and suspension
blocks.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, the classical Adams sequence has canonical isomorphisms
\[
E_\infty^{s,t}(X)\cong\operatorname{gr}_F^s\pi_{t-s}X.
\]
The isomorphisms identify the class of an infinite cycle represented by a tower lift with the associated graded class of the projection of that same lift. The tower of $\Sigma X$ is isomorphic stagewise and layerwise to the suspension of the tower of $X$. These isomorphisms commute with tower maps, the stage-zero comparison, and layer inclusions; the layer connecting maps commute with a minus sign under the suspension-interchange comparison.

\[

blocks.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:8e642612876d
blocks.title: Normalized synthetic lifts
blocks.body:
Let $X,Y\in\mathcal C_0$ and $f\colon X\to Y$. Put $\epsilon(f)=1$ if $f$ factors through the first stage of the target Adams tower, and put $\epsilon(f)=0$ otherwise. A normalized lift is a map
\[
\widehat f\colon\Sigma^{0,\epsilon(f)}\nu X\longrightarrow\nu Y
\]
such that $\widehat f\circ\lambda^{\epsilon(f)}=\nu(f)$, using the positive-target form of the power of $\lambda$.

blocks.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:5934d2f3caff
blocks.title: Point-set realizations, cofibers, and smash products
blocks.body:
The classical and synthetic categories have stable point-set model realizations whose homotopy categories are equivalent to $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $\mathrm{Syn}$, respectively. The classical model is closed symmetric monoidal, complete, cocomplete, and cofibrantly generated; its model tensor is compatible with the model structure. On cofibrant inputs, localization identifies its tensor with the tensor in $\mathrm{Sp}$, naturally in both inputs, and sends a cofibrant replacement of its unit to $S$.

Write $Q$ for passage from classical prespectra to $\mathrm{Sp}$ under the source equivalence. For well-based prespectra $X,Y$ and $f\colon X\to Y$, there is an isomorphism $Q\operatorname{Cone}(f)\cong C(Qf)$ commuting with the cone inclusion and boundary. For good based spaces $A,B$, there is a natural isomorphism $Q\Sigma^\infty A\otimes Q\Sigma^\infty B\cong Q\Sigma^\infty(A\wedge B)$ compatible with the left unit. For all prespectra $X,Y$, the tensor $QX\otimes QY$ is naturally isomorphic to $Q(RX\wedge_{\mathrm{diag}}RY)$, where $R$ is the good replacement functor.

blocks.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:e1d0c165854d
blocks.title: Recognition of classical stable homotopy
blocks.body: The ordinary stable localization of sequential prespectra is equivalent to $\mathrm{Sp}$. Under this equivalence, the source sphere corresponds to $S$, its identity to the positive sphere generator, and integer stable homotopy groups correspond naturally to the homotopy groups in $\mathrm{Sp}$, preserving zero and stable addition. The equivalence commutes naturally with desuspension and with suspension of well-based prespectra. A source mod-two coefficient prespectrum corresponds to $H\mathbb F_2$, with the same zeroth-homotopy coordinate, vanishing in nonzero degrees, and normalized coefficient unit.

blocks.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:b1eb322c2456
blocks.title: Associativity and units of mapping pairings
blocks.body:
For finite spectra $W,X,Y,Z$, page $r\in\mathbb Z$, and page classes $x\in M_r^i(W,X)$, $y\in M_r^j(X,Y)$, and $z\in M_r^k(Y,Z)$, one has
\[
P_r(P_r(x,y),z)=P_r(x,P_r(y,z))
\]
under the identifications of the two degree sums. For finite $X,Y$ and $x\in M_r^k(X,Y)$, the mapping-unit classes satisfy $P_r(u_X,x)=x=P_r(x,u_Y)$ under the zero-degree identifications. The abutment of $u_X$ corresponds to $\operatorname{id}_X\in\pi_0F(X,X)$.

blocks.title: Detection, products, and exactness of the synthetic analogue
blocks.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, $a,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$, the image of $K_{X,a,0}(x)$ under the first-quotient inclusion detects the inverse image of $x$ in $\pi_{t-s,t+a}((\Sigma^{0,a}\nu X)/\lambda)$.

For a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to\Sigma X$ whose mod-two homology is short exact in every degree, there is a boundary $\nu Z\to\Sigma\nu X$ making the images of its first two maps a distinguished synthetic triangle.

For $s,t\in\mathbb Z$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t}S^{0,0}$, the class $K_{S,k}(q\alpha)$ detects $\lambda^k\alpha$, where $q\alpha$ denotes the classical $E_2$ class obtained from $\alpha$ by the first-quotient comparison.

For $s,t,s',t',k,l\in\mathbb N$, $x\in E_2^{s,t}(S)$, and $y\in E_2^{s',t'}(S)$, if $K_{S,k}(x)$ detects $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t-k}S^{0,0}$ and $K_{S,l}(y)$ detects $\beta\in\pi_{t'-s',t'-l}S^{0,0}$, then $K_{S,k+l}(xy)$ detects $\alpha\beta$ after regrading the degree sums. For $\alpha\in\pi_{m,n}S^{0,0}$ and $\beta\in\pi_{k,l}S^{0,0}$, where $m,n,k,l\in\mathbb Z$, one has $\alpha\beta=(-1)^{mk}\beta\alpha$ after the sum-degree identifications.

blocks.title: Enriched composition and identities on pages and abutments
blocks.body:
Let $X,Y,Z$ be finite spectra, and identify their enriched hom objects with $M(X,Y)$, $M(Y,Z)$, and $M(X,Z)$. Write $c\colon M(X,Y)\otimes M(Y,Z)\to M(X,Z)$ for enriched composition. For $r\in\mathbb Z$, $i,j\in\mathbb Z^2$, and page classes $x,y$ of these degrees,
\[
c_r(T_r(x,y))=P_r(x,y).
\]
For $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and abutment elements $x,y$ of these degrees, one has $c_*(T_*(x,y))=P_*(x,y)$. The enriched identity $e_X\colon\mathbf1\to M(X,X)$ sends the tensor-unit class to the mapping unit on every page $r\in\mathbb Z$ and in the degree-zero abutment.

blocks.title: Filtration and normalization identities
blocks.body:
The following statements hold for the classical coefficient-unit tower and the source comparisons above.
\begin{itemize}
\item For finite $X,Y$, $f\colon X\to Y$, and $s\in\mathbb Z$, $f$ has map Adams filtration at least $s$ if and only if its corresponding class in $\pi_0F(X,Y)$ lies in $F^s$.
\item If $f\colon X\to X'$ and $g\colon Y\to Y'$ are stable equivalences of prespectra, then $Rf\wedge_{\mathrm{diag}}Rg$ is a stable equivalence.
\item For finite, rationally acyclic, homotopy two-local $X$ and $i\in\mathbb Z$, there exists $N\in\mathbb Z$ such that $F^s\pi_iX=0$ whenever $N<s$.
\item For $r,s\in\mathbb Z$, sphere braiding is multiplication by $(-1)^{rs}$ under the sphere-smash comparison with $S^{r+s}$.
\item For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and a first-layer element $z$ of the canonical sphere tower that is a cycle for page two, $\Phi_{s,t}$ sends the class of $z$, transported to the classical sphere sequence, to the Milnor cohomology class of $\phi_{s,t}(z)$.
\item One has $\Phi_{0,0}(1)=1_{\mathrm{Milnor}}$.
\item For $i\in\mathbb N$, one has $\Phi_{1,2^i}(h_i)=h_i^{\mathrm{Milnor}}$.
\end{itemize}

blocks.body:
Let $T$ be a coefficient-unit Adams tower, $r\geq2$, and $p=(s,t)\in\mathbb Z^2$. There exists a homomorphism
\[
d_r\colon E_r^p(T)\longrightarrow E_r^{p+(r,r-1)}(T)

blocks.title: Tower differential identities
blocks.body:
Let $T$ be a coefficient-unit Adams tower and $p\in\mathbb Z^2$. For every integer $r$, one has $d_r^2=0$. For $r\geq2$, with $n=r-2$ and quotient map $q\colon Z_n\to Z_n/B_n$, one has
\[
\ker d_r=\operatorname{im}(Z_{n+1}\longrightarrow Z_n/B_n),\qquad
\operatorname{im}d_r=\operatorname{im}(B_{n+1}\longrightarrow Z_n/B_n).
\]
The kernel formula is in degree $p$, and the image formula is in degree $p+(r,r-1)$.

    (hr : 2 ≤ r) :

    kernelSubobject (towerD T r p) =
      imageSubobject (Subobject.ofLE
        ((towerSSData T p).Z ↑(n + 1)) ((towerSSData T p).Z ↑n)
        ((towerSSData T p).Z_anti (by exact_mod_cast Nat.le_succ n)) ≫
        (towerSSData T p).pageπ ↑n) := by
  sorry

blocks.title: Weight maps preserve common representatives
blocks.body: Let $X\in\mathcal C_0$ and $s,t,w_1,w_2\in\mathbb Z$ with $w_1\leq w_2\leq t$. If $z\in E_\infty^{s,t,w_2}(\nu X)$ and the weight-$w_2$ synthetic label of $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ have a common infinite-cycle representative, then $W_{w_2,w_1}(z)$ and the weight-$w_1$ label of $x$ have a common infinite-cycle representative.
